model.why: gemini-3.8-flash's free-tier request quota is limit:20 and the 429 persisted past 5.5 minutes of silence — because 20 is a DAILY quota (RPD), not per-minute: Google's own public forum thread is titled 'Gemini 3.8 Flash Free Tier 20 RPD Is Too Limited for Practical Evaluation', and the rate-limits page states RPD resets at midnight Pacific. No amount of [המשך] could have finished the seeding that day on that model. The quota metric named in the 429 body is generate_content_free_tier_requests WITH THE MODEL ID INSIDE IT, so it is per-model ⇒ a different model draws a fresh bucket. gemini-3.5-flash-lite is the newest stable flash-lite (release notes: GA 21/07/2026, newer than gemini-3.1-flash-lite at 07/05/2026), the pricing page lists it as free-tier eligible, and the models page positions it as 'low-latency, highly cost-effective subagent option designed for high-volume automation'. Structured output: the structured-output page names no supported-model list and its only model restriction is 'This feature is available only to Gemini 3 series models' — flash-lite 3.5 is series 3. PROVEN LIVE: 386 notes, 13 requests, 0 refusals.
model.thinking_level: minimal — set, and set as a PER-MODEL MAP (THINKING_LEVEL_BY_MODEL), not a constant. The thinking page's per-model table gives gemini-3.5-flash-lite default 'minimal' and allows minimal|low|medium|high, but gives gemini-3.8-flash only low|medium|high — a hard-coded 'minimal' would have 400'd every batch the moment anyone set GEMINI_MODEL back to the old default. A model absent from the map is sent with no thinking_level at all.
